metadata.title: Freelancer Bookkeeping Service Platform Data Assets
metadata.description: Catalog of the client and access, expense and banking, sales and invoicing, ledger, filings and payroll, bookkeeper workflow and quality, and growth and client lifecycle data assets that power the Kees de Boekhouder and Founders bookkeeping-as-a-service model for more than 10,000 Dutch freelancers, VOFs and BVs, with AVG (GDPR) classification and BSN handling, PSD2 bank consent data through Ponto, the Dutch fiscal retention duty of 7 years (10 years for real-estate related VAT), filings to the Belastingdienst and KVK, EU data residency, backing stores and team ownership.

rootGroups.name: Client and Access Data
rootGroups.description: The data that says who a Kees de Boekhouder client is and who may act on their administration: the client account with its subscription and personal bookkeeper, the legal entity behind it (eenmanszaak, VOF, BV) with KVK number, VAT number and trading names, the user identities of clients and staff, and the audit trail that proves who saw and changed what. This is where the AVG obligation is concentrated: names, addresses, BSN and bank details of more than 10,000 entrepreneurs live here, and access is restricted to the assigned bookkeeper and authorised staff.

subGroups.name: Accounts, Identity and Audit
subGroups.description: The client account as the anchor of everything else, the user identities of clients, partners, bookkeepers and staff with their roles, and the append-only audit trail required for AVG accountability and fiscal reconstruction.

assets.name: Client Account
assets.description: One client relationship with Kees de Boekhouder or Founders: the entrepreneur's name, private and business address, date of birth and BSN (needed for the income tax return), contact details, the legal form and plan (eenmanszaak €840, VOF €1,140 for two partners plus €100 per extra partner, holding BV €1,750 or werkmaatschappij €2,450 per year ex VAT, invoiced monthly), the assigned personal bookkeeper and backup colleague, the office (Amsterdam, Rotterdam or Utrecht), the fiscal partner where a partner income tax return (€125 incl. VAT) is ordered, add-ons (bank connection, payroll), the start date of the first full fiscal year, cancellation notice status and the link to the KVK-registered entity. Created by Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching (onbd) after the mutual-fit check and mastered in Identity, Login and Access Control (iden).
assets.businessMeaning: The single client record that the app, the bookkeeper workspace, billing and the partner programme all hang from: if the account is wrong, the wrong bookkeeper checks the wrong entity and the wrong plan is invoiced.
assets.accessScope: the client for their own account; the assigned bookkeeper and backup colleague; client success and billing staff for lifecycle changes; BSN and date of birth masked outside the filing modules; never visible to other clients or partners

interfaces.name: client-account api
interfaces.description: Account creation, profile, legal-form and plan attributes, bookkeeper assignment, fiscal-partner and add-on flags, cancellation status and masked-BSN lookup API used by the client app, the bookkeeper workspace, billing, the partner programme and the network profiles.

interfaces.name: client account events
interfaces.description: Client activated, plan changed, bookkeeper reassigned, add-on enabled, cancellation notice received and account closed events consumed by workload planning, subscription billing, notifications, the partner programme and the audit trail.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the subscription and 7 years after the last fiscal year Kees filed for, because the account identifies the administration the Belastingdienst may still examine; BSN and date of birth removed 7 years after closure, marketing consents withdrawn immediately on request
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; identification data passed to the Belastingdienst only inside filed returns; name and e-mail shared with an ecosystem partner only when the client claims a member benefit and consents; never sold or shared between clients

assets.name: User Identity
assets.description: A login on mijn.keesdeboekhouder.nl or the mobile app: e-mail address, password hash, two-factor settings, device registrations and push tokens, the roles the person holds (client owner, VOF partner with shared access, DGA, bookkeeper, team lead, QA specialist, client success, billing, administrator), the client accounts or bookkeeper portfolio the person may open, session and refresh tokens, consent records for the privacy statement and processing agreement, invitation status and last sign-in. Managed by Identity, Login and Access Control (iden), consumed on every screen of the Mobile App Shell (mobi) and written into the Audit Trail, AVG Compliance and Retention (audt) for every privileged action.
assets.businessMeaning: The gate to 10,000 administrations full of bank data and tax returns: correct roles are what let a bookkeeper see only their own portfolio and a VOF partner see only the shared administration.
assets.accessScope: the user for their own profile and devices; administrators of the platform team for role management; client success for invitations and resets; credentials and tokens never readable by anyone

interfaces.name: identity api
interfaces.description: Authentication, two-factor enrolment, session and refresh tokens, device and push-token registration, role and portfolio authorisation checks, invitation and password-reset API used by every client and workspace module and by the mobile shell.

interfaces.name: identity events
interfaces.description: User invited, activated, role granted or revoked, device registered, suspicious sign-in and account deactivated events consumed by the audit trail, security monitoring, notifications and client success.

governance.retention: kept while the user is active and 2 years after deactivation so the audit trail can still be attributed; session tokens expire per policy and sign-in logs are kept 12 months; device and push registrations deleted when the user removes the device
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; push tokens shared with the mobile platform providers for delivery only; never shared with partners or the Belastingdienst; a VOF partner's login sees only the administrations explicitly shared with them

assets.name: Audit Trail Entry
assets.description: An immutable record of one action on the platform: who (client, bookkeeper, staff member or system job), when, on which client account and object (booking, invoice, bank connection, return, message, allocation), the before and after values or a hash of a document, the channel (web, mobile, e-mail-in, Ponto sync, filing gateway, KVK, payment provider) and the legal basis where personal data was read outside the normal workflow, for example a backup bookkeeper opening a colleague's client file. Written by Audit Trail, AVG Compliance and Retention (audt) for every module and by the Integration and API Gateway (intg) for every external call, and the source for AVG access reconstruction, data-subject requests and retention execution.
assets.businessMeaning: The evidence that the AVG promise on the website is real: access is restricted to authorised staff, and every look into a client's administration can be reconstructed if the client or the authority asks.
assets.accessScope: the platform and security team and the Head of QA for investigations; the client for a report of who accessed their own administration on request; append-only, no edit or delete rights for anyone

interfaces.name: audit-trail api
interfaces.description: Append-only write and filtered read API (by actor, client account, object, period and channel) used by every module, the integration gateway, the AVG access-report function, data-subject request handling and the retention scheduler.

interfaces.name: audit events
interfaces.description: Privileged access, bulk export, retention deletion executed, consent withdrawn and integration failure events consumed by security monitoring, the QA team and operational dashboards.

governance.retention: entries on bookings, returns and filings kept 7 years after the fiscal year in line with the fiscal retention duty; access and sign-in entries kept 2 years; entries referencing deleted client data pseudonymised rather than removed so the chain of custody stays intact
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; extracts provided to the client for their own administration and to authorities on a lawful request only; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Entity Profile and Insight
subGroups.description: The legal entity behind the account with its KVK, VAT and trading-name data, the real-time dashboard snapshot the client sees on web and mobile, and the deadline reminders and notifications that keep the client and bookkeeper on time.

assets.name: Business Entity Profile
assets.description: The legal entity whose administration is kept: legal form (eenmanszaak, VOF, holding BV, werkmaatschappij), KVK number and registration date, statutory name and the multiple trading names the client may invoice under, VAT identification number and VAT filing frequency, KOR status (small business scheme up to €20,000 turnover), SBI activity codes, business address, IBANs used for the business, the partners of a VOF with their profit-share percentages, the DGA and shareholders of a BV, the fiscal year and the ledger scheme the bookkeeper applies. Synchronised with the Handelsregister by KVK Filing and Company Data (kvkf), applied by General Ledger and Booking Rules (ledg), printed on every invoice by Invoices, Credit Notes and Trading Names (invc) and used by the Document Archive (docs) to file documents per entity.
assets.businessMeaning: Legal form and VAT status decide almost every fiscal rule applied downstream: which return is filed, whether KOR applies, how VOF profit is split and whether the client belongs with Kees or with Founders.
assets.accessScope: the client and their VOF partners or co-shareholders; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; the bookkeeping engine team for scheme configuration; KVK data treated as public, private addresses and IBANs treated as personal data

interfaces.name: business-entity api
interfaces.description: Entity, legal form, KVK and VAT attributes, trading names, VOF partner shares, KOR status and ledger-scheme API used by the ledger, VAT and income tax preparation, invoicing, the document archive, onboarding and the Founders BV service.

interfaces.name: entity change events
interfaces.description: Trading name added, legal form changed (for example eenmanszaak to BV), VAT status or KOR changed, partner added or left and KVK data refreshed events consumed by the ledger, invoicing, subscription billing and the bookkeeper workspace.

interfaces.name: kvk extract exchange
interfaces.description: Handelsregister extracts retrieved through the KVK connection and stored with the entity, and the entity data sheet exported for the annual accounts and the switch to Founders.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the client relationship and 7 years after the last fiscal year filed; historical trading names and legal forms versioned per fiscal year because returns must be reproducible as filed
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; KVK number, trading names and VAT number appear on invoices sent to the client's customers; entity data included in filings to the Belastingdienst and KVK; never shared with ecosystem partners without the client's request

assets.name: Dashboard Snapshot
assets.description: The materialised view behind the client dashboard on web and mobile: revenue per quarter and year to date, cost categories with totals, investments and depreciation, provisional profit, VAT to pay or receive per quarter, an indicative income tax reservation, open quotes and unpaid invoices, unmatched bank transactions, documents awaiting bookkeeper review and the next deadlines, recalculated in near real time when a booking, invoice, match or bookkeeper correction is posted. Produced by the Financial Dashboard and Quarterly Results (dash) from ledger entries and shown together with the VAT Position and Tax Reservation View.
assets.businessMeaning: The promise on the website made visible: direct insight into revenue, costs, profit and VAT per quarter without the client ever opening a ledger, which is why the numbers must match what the bookkeeper will file.
assets.accessScope: the client and their VOF partners for the own entity; the assigned bookkeeper for coaching the client on open items; product analytics only in aggregated, pseudonymised form

interfaces.name: dashboard api
interfaces.description: Per-entity quarter and year figures, cost-category breakdowns, VAT position, tax reservation indication, open items and next-deadline API read by the web dashboard, the mobile app and the bookkeeper's client file overview.

interfaces.name: dashboard refresh events
interfaces.description: Snapshot recalculated, quarter closed by the bookkeeper and figure materially changed events consumed by push notifications, the VAT view and product analytics.

governance.retention: rebuildable at any time from the ledger; snapshots kept per quarter for 2 years to explain what the client saw at a given moment, then dropped; not a fiscal record
governance.sharingPolicy: visible only to the client, their partners and their bookkeeper; aggregated benchmarks (for example average revenue per creative freelancer) only in anonymised form for content and growth; never shared with partners

assets.name: Notification
assets.description: One message pushed to a client or bookkeeper through the app, push notification or e-mail: the reminder that the quarterly VAT return is due on the last day of the month after the quarter, that Ponto re-authorisation is needed within the 90 to 180 day window, that receipts are missing for a bank transaction, that an invoice is overdue and a reminder was sent, that the bookkeeper has questions before closing the quarter, that the income tax return is ready to approve, or that a rule change (zelfstandigenaftrek, KOR, Wet DBA) affects the client; with template, channel, delivery status, read state and the deep link into the app. Composed by Deadlines, To-dos and Notifications (ntfy), triggered by Payment Tracking and Reminders (dunn) and delivered through the Mobile App Shell (mobi).
assets.businessMeaning: The proactive updates about changes and deadlines that clients name as a reason to stay with a personal bookkeeper, and the nudges that get receipts and answers in before the filing deadline.
assets.accessScope: the recipient; the assigned bookkeeper for the notifications sent to their clients; the client app team for template and delivery diagnostics without message bodies

interfaces.name: notification api
interfaces.description: Template rendering, scheduling, channel selection, delivery status, read-state and preference API used by the deadline orchestration, payment reminders, bank re-authorisation prompts, the bookkeeper workspace and the mobile app.

interfaces.name: notification events
interfaces.description: Notification scheduled, delivered, opened, action completed and delivery failed events consumed by the to-do list, deadline escalation to the bookkeeper and engagement analytics.

governance.retention: kept 12 months for support and engagement analysis, then deleted; notifications that constitute a client approval (for example approving a return for filing) are referenced from the audit trail and follow its 7-year retention
governance.sharingPolicy: delivered only to the recipient through the channels they enabled; e-mail and push providers act as processors; never shared with partners

rootGroups.name: Expense and Banking Data
rootGroups.description: The data that captures the administration at the source: photographed and e-mailed receipts and purchase invoices recognised by Scan & Herken, the expense bookings derived from them, the PSD2 bank connections through Ponto, the transactions synchronised four times a day and the matches between transactions and bookings. This is where bookkeeper productivity is won or lost: every receipt recognised correctly and every transaction matched automatically is a booking the bookkeeper only has to check, not make.

subGroups.name: Receipts and Expenses
subGroups.description: The source documents and the expense bookings that come out of them, from photo to categorised, VAT-coded booking ready for review.

assets.name: Receipt Document
assets.description: A receipt, purchase invoice or other source document uploaded by photo from the mobile app, file upload on the web, or forwarding to the client's personal e-mail-in address: the original image or PDF, the recognised fields (supplier, date, invoice number, amounts, VAT rate and amount, currency, payment method), recognition confidence per field, duplicate detection result, the client's chosen category, the link to the expense booking it produced and to the bank transaction that paid it, and the review status of the bookkeeper. Captured by Scan & Herken Receipt Capture and Recognition (scan) and kept per entity and fiscal year in the Document Archive (docs) as the fiscal evidence behind every deduction and VAT reclaim.
assets.businessMeaning: The original evidence the Belastingdienst can ask for behind any cost or VAT deduction; recognition quality on these documents is the biggest lever on both client effort and bookkeeper review time.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists during four-eyes checks; recognition engineers only on samples the client consented to or on synthetic data

interfaces.name: receipt-document api
interfaces.description: Upload, e-mail-in ingestion, recognition result, field correction, duplicate check, category suggestion, archive retrieval and review-status API used by the mobile app, the web app, the expense booking module and the bookkeeper's client file.

interfaces.name: receipt events
interfaces.description: Document received, recognised, low-confidence flagged, corrected by client, duplicate detected and archived events consumed by expense booking, bank matching, notifications and recognition-quality analytics.

interfaces.name: receipt originals
interfaces.description: Images and PDFs from camera, file upload and e-mail forwarding, and per-fiscal-year ZIP exports of all source documents for the client, an auditor or the switch to another bookkeeper.

governance.retention: kept at least 7 years after the end of the fiscal year under the Dutch fiscal retention duty, 10 years where the document concerns immovable property for VAT purposes; deleted after that unless the client exports or asks to keep it
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the client and Kees de Boekhouder; originals provided to the Belastingdienst only in an audit and to the client's next bookkeeper on request; recognition provider, if external, bound by a processor agreement with no training on client documents

assets.name: Expense Booking
assets.description: A cost or investment booking proposed from a recognised receipt or entered by the client: supplier, date, description, net amount, VAT rate and deductible VAT (including partially deductible and private-use items such as a car or phone), cost category from the ledger scheme, investment flag with depreciation schedule for assets above the threshold, the source document and bank transaction it links to, whether the client or the bookkeeper created it, and the review state (proposed, accepted by client, checked by bookkeeper, corrected, rejected). Created in Expense and Purchase Booking (expn) from Scan & Herken (scan) output and posted as a ledger entry by General Ledger and Booking Rules once accepted.
assets.businessMeaning: The booking that turns a photo into a deduction: getting the category and VAT right here is what makes the quarterly VAT return and the year-end close a check instead of a rebuild.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners; the assigned bookkeeper and backup for review and correction; QA specialists for four-eyes samples; the bookkeeping engine team for rule diagnostics without client identification

interfaces.name: expense-booking api
interfaces.description: Booking proposal, category and VAT rule application, private-use split, investment and depreciation, review-state transition and bulk-correction API used by the client app, Scan & Herken, bank matching, the ledger and the bookkeeper's review queue.

interfaces.name: expense booking events
interfaces.description: Booking proposed, accepted by client, checked or corrected by bookkeeper, rejected and investment registered events consumed by the ledger, the dashboard, the review queue and productivity analytics.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year (10 years for immovable-property VAT items) as part of the administration; corrections keep the original version so every filed figure can be traced back
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the client and Kees de Boekhouder; totals flow into VAT and income tax returns filed with the Belastingdienst; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Bank Connections and Matching
subGroups.description: The PSD2 consents through Ponto, the bank transactions synchronised four times a day from Knab, Rabobank, ABN AMRO, bunq and other connected banks, and the matches that reconcile them with bookings and invoices.

assets.name: Bank Connection
assets.description: A PSD2 account-information consent between a client's business bank account and the platform through Ponto (Isabel Group): bank and IBAN, account holder, consent granted date and the expiry that requires re-authorisation every 90 to 180 days depending on the bank, the Ponto integration identifiers and access token reference (stored in the vault, never in the record), sync schedule (four times a day), last successful sync and error state, the €5 per month per connected account add-on link to the subscription, and the entity the account belongs to. Managed by Bank Connection (bank) and executed through the Integration and API Gateway (intg).
assets.businessMeaning: The consent that makes the administration almost effortless: a live bank feed means the client stops typing transactions, so consent expiry is the most common reason a dashboard goes stale.
assets.accessScope: the client for their own accounts; the assigned bookkeeper sees connection status and IBAN only; the expenses and banking team and platform team for sync diagnostics; tokens readable by the sync service alone

interfaces.name: bank-connection api
interfaces.description: Consent initiation and Ponto redirect, re-authorisation, account listing, sync scheduling and status, revocation and add-on activation API used by the client app, the mobile app, subscription billing and the integration gateway.

interfaces.name: bank connection events
interfaces.description: Consent granted, sync completed or failed, consent expiring in 14 days, consent expired, account revoked and add-on billed events consumed by notifications, transaction matching, subscription billing and the bookkeeper's client file.

governance.retention: consent and connection metadata kept while the account is connected and 7 years after as part of the administration's audit trail; access tokens deleted immediately on revocation or expiry; Ponto identifiers retained only as long as needed for reconciliation with Ponto invoices
governance.sharingPolicy: consent data exchanged with Ponto (Isabel Group) as the licensed PSD2 provider and with the client's bank; never shared with partners; the Belastingdienst receives figures, not connections

assets.name: Bank Transaction
assets.description: One transaction synchronised from a connected business bank account: booking date and value date, amount and currency, counterparty name and IBAN, remittance information and structured references, bank transaction code, running balance, the Ponto transaction identifier for idempotent syncs, and the platform's derived attributes such as detected invoice number, suggested category, private-transaction flag and the match state (unmatched, auto-matched, manually matched, booked directly). Pulled four times a day by Bank Connection (bank) and consumed by the Transaction Matching Engine (mtch); counterparties on the client's private account are visible only when the client connects that account deliberately.
assets.businessMeaning: The most complete record of what actually happened financially in the business: the feed that lets the bookkeeper spot missing receipts and undeclared revenue before the VAT return goes out.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners for the own accounts; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists for four-eyes samples; matching-rule engineers on pseudonymised data only

interfaces.name: bank-transaction api
interfaces.description: Transaction listing per account and period, unmatched-item queue, counterparty and reference search, private-flagging, direct-booking and idempotent sync-ingest API used by the client app, the matching engine, the dashboard and the bookkeeper's review queue.

interfaces.name: bank transaction events
interfaces.description: Transactions synced, unmatched transaction older than 30 days, large or unusual transaction detected and transaction flagged private events consumed by matching, notifications, the dashboard and the review queue.

interfaces.name: bank statement exchange
interfaces.description: CAMT and CSV statement imports for periods before the Ponto connection or for banks without a connection, and per-fiscal-year transaction exports for the annual accounts and audits.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year as part of the administration under the fiscal retention duty; transactions flagged private by the client excluded from the ledger but retained in the raw feed for reconciliation
governance.sharingPolicy: received from the client's bank through Ponto under the client's PSD2 consent; visible to the client and their bookkeeper only; aggregated into returns for the Belastingdienst; never shared with partners or used for marketing

assets.name: Transaction Match
assets.description: The reconciliation between a bank transaction and one or more bookings or invoices: the matched expense booking, sales invoice, payslip payment, VAT payment to the Belastingdienst, subscription debit or transfer between own accounts, the match type (automatic by amount and reference, automatic by learned counterparty rule, manual by client, manual by bookkeeper, direct booking created from the transaction), confidence, partial-payment and rounding-difference handling, who confirmed it and when, and the unmatch history. Produced by the Transaction Matching Engine (mtch) and posted as ledger entries by General Ledger and Booking Rules; automatic match rate per client is a core bookkeeper productivity metric.
assets.businessMeaning: Every automatic match is a booking nobody had to make; the match rate decides how many clients a bookkeeper can serve well and how quickly a quarter is ready to file.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; the expenses and banking team for rule tuning on pseudonymised samples

interfaces.name: transaction-match api
interfaces.description: Match suggestion, confirm, unmatch, split and partial-payment, learned counterparty rule and direct-booking API used by the client app, the mobile app, the bookkeeper's review queue and the ledger.

interfaces.name: match events
interfaces.description: Auto-matched, manually matched, unmatched, rule learned and invoice paid-by-match events consumed by the ledger, payment tracking, the dashboard and productivity analytics.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year with the ledger entries it explains; learned counterparty rules kept while the client is active and deleted with the account
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the client and Kees de Boekhouder; never leaves the platform except as the ledger figures inside returns

rootGroups.name: Sales and Invoicing Data
rootGroups.description: The revenue side of the administration: quotes and proposals, invoices and credit notes issued under one of the client's trading names with the correct Dutch VAT treatment (21%, 9%, 0%, reverse charge, KOR exempt), the customers they are sent to, and the payment status that drives reminders. Because Kees does not accept external accounting software, every invoice a client sends is created here and lands directly in the ledger and the VAT return.

subGroups.name: Quotes and Invoices
subGroups.description: The documents the client sends to get paid, with status tracking from draft to paid and the VAT logic that keeps them compliant.

assets.name: Quote
assets.description: A quote or proposal sent to a prospective customer of the client: quote number, the trading name and layout used, customer, line items with descriptions, quantities, unit prices and VAT rates, validity period, terms and attachments, the PDF as sent, delivery by e-mail with open tracking, the status (draft, sent, viewed, accepted, declined, expired) and the invoice it was converted into. Created in Quotes and Proposals (quot), shared with the Invoices module for one-click conversion, and shown on the dashboard as expected revenue for the creative and knowledge freelancers who quote before they work.
assets.businessMeaning: The start of the revenue pipeline for freelancers who win work by proposal: conversion to an invoice without retyping is what makes the quoting step worth doing inside the bookkeeping app.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners; the assigned bookkeeper for context on expected revenue; the invoicing team for template diagnostics without customer data

interfaces.name: quote api
interfaces.description: Quote drafting, line items and VAT calculation, PDF rendering per trading name, e-mail delivery with tracking, status transitions and convert-to-invoice API used by the web and mobile app and the dashboard.

interfaces.name: quote events
interfaces.description: Quote sent, viewed, accepted, declined, expired and converted events consumed by invoicing, the dashboard's expected-revenue figure and notifications.

interfaces.name: quote pdf outputs
interfaces.description: PDF renditions per trading name and language sent to the customer by e-mail or downloaded by the client, and CSV export of the quote pipeline.

governance.retention: kept while the client is active and 2 years after the quote expired or was declined; quotes converted into invoices follow the invoice's 7-year retention because they document the agreed price
governance.sharingPolicy: sent to the client's customer at the client's instruction; visible to the client and their bookkeeper; never shared with partners

assets.name: Sales Invoice
assets.description: An invoice or credit note issued by the client: sequential invoice number per trading name, invoice and due date, the customer with their VAT number where reverse charge applies, line items, VAT per rate (21%, 9%, 0%, reverse charge within the EU, exempt under KOR), totals, payment reference and IBAN, the PDF as sent, delivery channel and open tracking, payment status (draft, sent, partially paid, paid, overdue, credited, written off), the bank transaction that settled it, reminder history and the revenue and VAT ledger entries it generated. Issued by Invoices, Credit Notes and Trading Names (invc), followed up by Payment Tracking and Reminders (dunn) and filed per entity in the archive as the sales side of the administration.
assets.businessMeaning: Where the client's revenue is born and where the VAT return's output tax comes from: invoice compliance here is what keeps the VAT return correct and the Belastingdienst quiet.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists for four-eyes samples; the invoicing team for numbering and template diagnostics without customer data

interfaces.name: sales-invoice api
interfaces.description: Invoice and credit note creation, numbering per trading name, VAT and reverse-charge rules, PDF rendering, e-mail delivery, payment status, reminder scheduling and ledger posting API used by the web and mobile app, payment tracking, matching and the ledger.

interfaces.name: invoice events
interfaces.description: Invoice sent, viewed, due, overdue, paid, partially paid, credited and written off events consumed by payment reminders, bank matching, the dashboard, the VAT return and notifications.

interfaces.name: invoice outputs
interfaces.description: PDF invoices and credit notes per trading name, UBL e-invoice export for customers who require it, and per-fiscal-year sales ledger exports for annual accounts, audits and the switch to another bookkeeper.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year under the fiscal retention duty (10 years for invoices concerning immovable property); issued invoices immutable, corrections only by credit note
governance.sharingPolicy: sent to the client's customer; visible to the client and their bookkeeper; totals reported to the Belastingdienst in VAT returns and, for EU reverse-charge sales, the ICP declaration; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Customers and Debtors
subGroups.description: The client's own customers as they appear on quotes, invoices and reminders, the one place the platform holds personal data of people who are not Kees clients.

assets.name: Customer Contact
assets.description: A customer of the client (a debtor) as used on quotes and invoices: company or private name, contact person, e-mail address for delivery, postal address, KVK and VAT number where applicable (needed for EU reverse-charge invoices), default payment terms and language, the trading name the client uses for them, the open balance and payment behaviour derived from invoices, and the reminder preferences. Maintained in Invoices, Credit Notes and Trading Names (invc), reused by Quotes and Proposals (quot), and never enriched from external sources beyond a KVK lookup the client initiates.
assets.businessMeaning: The address book that makes invoicing a two-click job and the place where the platform holds data about people who never signed up with Kees, which sets the bar for minimisation.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners; the assigned bookkeeper sees names and balances for review; the invoicing team only for deduplication diagnostics without personal fields

interfaces.name: customer-contact api
interfaces.description: Contact creation, KVK lookup, VAT number validation for reverse charge, merge and deduplication, balance and payment-behaviour summary API used by quotes, invoices, payment reminders and the mobile app.

interfaces.name: customer contact events
interfaces.description: Contact created, merged, VAT number validated and balance changed events consumed by invoicing, payment reminders and the dashboard.

governance.retention: kept while the client uses the contact and 7 years after the last invoice to that customer, because the contact identifies the counterparty on retained invoices; deleted with the client's data after the retention period
governance.sharingPolicy: processed on behalf of the client as controller under the processing agreement; shared only with e-mail delivery providers as processors; never used by Kees for marketing or shared with partners

rootGroups.name: Ledger, Filings and Payroll Data
rootGroups.description: The bookkeeping engine's own records: the general ledger built from accepted bookings, matches and invoices, the quarterly VAT returns, the annual accounts with deductions applied (zelfstandigenaftrek, startersaftrek, mkb-winstvrijstelling), the income tax returns of clients and their fiscal partners, the corporate tax returns and statutory accounts of BV clients served by Founders, the payslips of small employers and DGAs, and the submissions that go to the Belastingdienst and KVK through the official digital channels. These are the records the company carries fiscal responsibility for, with the heaviest retention and confidentiality obligations in the domain.

subGroups.name: Ledger and Returns
subGroups.description: From ledger entries to filed returns: the VAT return per quarter, the year-end close and annual accounts, and the income and corporate tax returns prepared by the bookkeeper and approved by the client.

assets.name: Ledger Entry
assets.description: A double-entry posting in the client's general ledger: fiscal year and period, journal (sales, purchases, bank, memorial, payroll, year-end), ledger account from the scheme for the legal form, debit and credit amounts, VAT code and amount, cost or revenue category for the dashboard, the source object (expense booking, sales invoice, transaction match, payslip, depreciation run or bookkeeper correction), the partner allocation for a VOF, the private-use share, lock state per quarter once the VAT return is filed, and the bookkeeper who posted or corrected it. Mastered by General Ledger and Booking Rules (ledg), fed by Expense and Purchase Booking (expn) and the Transaction Matching Engine (mtch), and read by the dashboard, the VAT view, VAT return preparation and the year-end close.
assets.businessMeaning: The administration itself in the legal sense: what the Belastingdienst may examine for seven years and what every return, annual account and dashboard number is derived from.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners read their own ledger through the dashboard; the assigned bookkeeper and backup post and correct; QA specialists and the Head of QA for four-eyes checks; the bookkeeping engine team for scheme and rule maintenance on pseudonymised data

interfaces.name: ledger api
interfaces.description: Posting, correction with reversal, period lock and unlock, trial balance, ledger-account and category reporting, VOF partner allocation and depreciation-run API used by expense booking, matching, invoicing, payroll, the dashboard, VAT return preparation and the year-end close.

interfaces.name: ledger events
interfaces.description: Entry posted, corrected, period locked after filing, quarter checked by bookkeeper and year closed events consumed by the dashboard snapshot, the VAT view, deadline orchestration, QA sampling and productivity analytics.

interfaces.name: ledger exports
interfaces.description: Auditfile (XAF) and CSV exports of the full ledger per fiscal year for the client, an auditor, the Belastingdienst in an examination or the client's next bookkeeper.

governance.retention: kept at least 7 years after the end of the fiscal year under the Dutch fiscal retention duty and 10 years for entries concerning immovable property for VAT; locked periods immutable, corrections only by dated reversal so filed figures remain reproducible
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the client and Kees de Boekhouder or Founders; aggregated into returns for the Belastingdienst; complete ledger handed to the client or their next bookkeeper on request; never shared with partners

assets.name: VAT Return
assets.description: The quarterly (or, for some entities, monthly or yearly) turnover tax return of one entity: the period, the boxes of the Belastingdienst form (domestic supplies per rate, reverse-charged supplies and purchases, intra-EU supplies and acquisitions, import, input VAT, KOR exemption), the amounts derived from locked ledger periods, the reconciliation to sales invoices and expense bookings, the bookkeeper's check notes, the client's approval, the submission reference and acknowledgement from the Belastingdienst, the payment or refund due with the deadline on the last day of the month after the quarter, the related ICP declaration where applicable, and any supplementary return (suppletie). Prepared in VAT Return Preparation (vatr), shown to the client in the VAT Position and Tax Reservation View (vatv) and filed through the Belastingdienst Filing Gateway (bdgw).
assets.businessMeaning: The most frequent moment of truth for the fixed-fee promise: four times a year every client's return must go out on time and right, and a late or wrong return is a fine the client blames the bookkeeper for.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners for approval and the filed copy; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists for four-eyes checks; the filing team for submission diagnostics without amounts

interfaces.name: vat-return api
interfaces.description: Return calculation from locked periods, box-level reconciliation, bookkeeper check notes, client approval, submission hand-off, acknowledgement and payment-due API used by the VAT view, the bookkeeper workspace, the filing gateway, deadline orchestration and notifications.

interfaces.name: vat return events
interfaces.description: Return prepared, approved by client, submitted, acknowledged, payment due and supplementary return needed events consumed by the dashboard, notifications, deadline orchestration, QA and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: vat return outputs
interfaces.description: The return as filed in the Belastingdienst digital format and a PDF copy for the client, plus the ICP declaration and the quarterly VAT specification exported for the annual accounts.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year (10 years where immovable-property VAT is involved) together with the acknowledgement, because the filed return is the primary evidence in a VAT examination; supplementary returns kept with the original
governance.sharingPolicy: filed with the Belastingdienst through the official digital channel under the company's intermediary authorisation; copy visible to the client and their bookkeeper; never shared with partners

assets.name: Annual Accounts
assets.description: The year-end result of one entity for one fiscal year: the closed ledger with year-end journal entries (depreciation, provisions, private use, stock, accruals), the balance sheet and profit and loss statement, the fiscal profit calculation with the hours criterion assessment and deductions applied (zelfstandigenaftrek €1,200 in 2026 falling to €900 in 2027, startersaftrek €2,123 where eligible, mkb-winstvrijstelling), the VOF profit split per partner, the investment and depreciation schedule, the bookkeeper's closing checklist and the client's approval, and for BV clients the statutory annual accounts in the format required for the KVK filing. Produced by Year-end Close and Annual Accounts (yend) and consumed by Income Tax Return (IB) Preparation (itax) and Corporate Tax (VPB) and BV Statutory Accounts (ctax).
assets.businessMeaning: The document that converts a year of bookings into taxable profit: getting the deductions and the hours criterion right here is where a personal bookkeeper visibly earns the yearly fee.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners for approval and the final document; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists for four-eyes checks before approval; Founders bookkeepers for BV entities; banks or mortgage advisers only when the client sends the document themselves

interfaces.name: annual-accounts api
interfaces.description: Year-end journal generation, closing checklist, fiscal profit and deduction calculation, VOF profit split, statutory-format rendering, approval and versioning API used by the year-end close, income and corporate tax preparation, the bookkeeper workspace and the client app.

interfaces.name: year-end events
interfaces.description: Year-end started, checklist item completed, four-eyes check passed, accounts approved by client and year closed events consumed by income tax preparation, corporate tax preparation, deadline orchestration and productivity analytics.

interfaces.name: annual accounts outputs
interfaces.description: PDF annual accounts and fiscal profit statement for the client, the statutory annual accounts for KVK deposit in the required digital format, and the year-end package handed to the client's next bookkeeper or a lender.

governance.retention: kept at least 7 years after the end of the fiscal year (10 years where immovable property is on the balance sheet) as part of the administration; approved versions immutable; earlier drafts kept until approval and then reduced to the audit trail
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the client and Kees de Boekhouder or Founders; figures flow into income and corporate tax returns filed with the Belastingdienst and, for BVs, the statutory accounts deposited at KVK; given to lenders, mortgage advisers or partners only when the client shares them

assets.name: Income Tax Return
assets.description: The income tax (inkomstenbelasting) return of a client or, at €125 incl. VAT, of their fiscal partner for one tax year: BSN, personal and partner data, the business profit from the annual accounts with the entrepreneur deductions, income from employment for starters combining a job with their business, home-ownership and mortgage data, other income and assets in box 3, allocation of joint items between fiscal partners, preliminary assessments received, the bookkeeper's notes and questions to the client, the client's approval, the filed return and the Belastingdienst acknowledgement, and the final assessment when it arrives. Prepared in Income Tax Return (IB) Preparation (itax) from the annual accounts and filed through the Belastingdienst Filing Gateway (bdgw).
assets.businessMeaning: The annual promise that every client gets their return filed right and on time, and the most sensitive document in the domain because it combines BSN, income, home and family data of the client and their partner.
assets.accessScope: the client and, for their own return, the fiscal partner; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists for four-eyes checks; BSN visible only inside the preparation and filing modules and masked elsewhere

interfaces.name: income-tax-return api
interfaces.description: Return preparation from annual accounts, prefilled data intake, fiscal-partner allocation, deduction and credit calculation, question-to-client workflow, approval, submission hand-off and assessment registration API used by the bookkeeper workspace, the client app, the filing gateway and deadline orchestration.

interfaces.name: income tax events
interfaces.description: Return prepared, questions sent to client, approved, submitted, acknowledged, preliminary assessment received and final assessment received events consumed by notifications, deadline orchestration, QA sampling and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: income tax outputs
interfaces.description: The return in the Belastingdienst digital format as filed, a PDF copy and a summary for the client and their partner, and the prior-year return copies imported when a client switches to Kees.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the tax year, covering the Belastingdienst's reassessment period; BSN and partner data removed from copies when the retention period ends; drafts and questions kept until filing and then reduced to the audit trail
governance.sharingPolicy: filed with the Belastingdienst through the official digital channel under the company's intermediary authorisation; shared only with the client and their fiscal partner for their own return; never shared with partners or used for marketing

assets.name: Corporate Tax Return
assets.description: The corporate income tax (vennootschapsbelasting) return and statutory filing package of a BV client served by Founders for one fiscal year: RSIN and fiscal number of the holding or werkmaatschappij, the fiscal profit reconciliation from the statutory annual accounts, participation exemption and intercompany positions between holding and operating company, DGA customary salary and current-account positions, dividend withholding tax where a dividend is paid, loss carry-forward, the preliminary and final assessments, the client's approval, the filed return and acknowledgement, and the statutory annual accounts deposited at KVK within the legal deadline. Prepared in Corporate Tax (VPB) and BV Statutory Accounts (ctax) by Founders bookkeepers from the annual accounts and filed through the Belastingdienst Filing Gateway and KVK Filing and Company Data.
assets.businessMeaning: The compliance package that makes the Founders fixed fee (holding €1,750, werkmaatschappij €2,450 per year) credible and the reason a growing freelancer can move to a BV without leaving the brand.
assets.accessScope: the DGA and co-shareholders of the BV; the Founders bookkeeper and backup; QA specialists for four-eyes checks; the filing team for submission and KVK deposit diagnostics without amounts

interfaces.name: corporate-tax-return api
interfaces.description: Fiscal profit reconciliation, participation and intercompany positions, DGA salary and current-account checks, dividend tax, loss carry-forward, approval, submission hand-off and KVK deposit status API used by the Founders workspace, the client app, the filing gateway and KVK filing.

interfaces.name: corporate tax events
interfaces.description: Return prepared, approved, submitted, acknowledged, statutory accounts deposited at KVK and assessment received events consumed by notifications, deadline orchestration, QA sampling and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: corporate tax outputs
interfaces.description: The VPB return in the Belastingdienst digital format, the statutory annual accounts in the KVK deposit format, and PDF copies for the DGA and the BV's board.

governance.retention: kept at least 7 years after the end of the fiscal year (10 years where the BV holds immovable property) with the acknowledgement and KVK deposit confirmation; approved versions immutable
governance.sharingPolicy: filed with the Belastingdienst and deposited at KVK, where the statutory accounts become public in the Handelsregister; internal to the DGA, Founders and the Kees platform otherwise; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Payroll and Authority Filings
subGroups.description: The payslips of clients with employees or a DGA salary, and the submissions that carry every return, declaration and deposit to the Belastingdienst and KVK through the official digital channels.

assets.name: Payslip
assets.description: One monthly payslip of an employee or DGA of a client, produced at €17.50 per payslip per employee per month: employee identity with BSN and date of birth, employment contract data (start date, hours, wage scale, DGA customary-salary flag), gross salary, allowances and deductions, wage tax and national insurance contributions, employee insurance premiums, pension and holiday allowance reservations, net pay and payment IBAN, the wage tax return (loonaangifte) period the payslip belongs to, the payroll journal entries posted to the ledger, the annual wage statement, and the identity document copy and wage tax declaration collected at the start of employment. Produced by Payroll and Payslips (payr) for VOFs with staff and for BV clients of Founders, with the wage tax return filed as a submission through the Belastingdienst gateway.
assets.businessMeaning: The add-on that keeps small employers and DGAs on the platform: payroll data is the most regulated personal data Kees processes and is what makes the VOF-to-BV path complete.
assets.accessScope: the employer client and DGA for their own payroll; the employee for their own payslips; the payroll bookkeeper in the bookkeeping pods and the Founders team; BSN and identity copies visible only in the payroll module

interfaces.name: payroll api
interfaces.description: Employee onboarding, contract and wage data, monthly payroll run, payslip rendering, wage tax return preparation, payroll journal posting, annual wage statement and DGA customary-salary check API used by the payroll module, the ledger, the filing gateway, subscription billing and the client app.

interfaces.name: payroll events
interfaces.description: Employee added or left, payroll run completed, payslip delivered, wage tax return submitted and DGA salary below customary threshold events consumed by the ledger, the filing gateway, subscription billing (per-payslip fee) and notifications.

interfaces.name: payroll outputs
interfaces.description: PDF payslips and annual wage statements for employees, the wage tax return in the Belastingdienst digital format, SEPA payment files for net salaries where the client uses them, and payroll exports for pension providers and the annual accounts.

governance.retention: payroll administration kept 7 years after the end of the fiscal year under the fiscal retention duty; identity document copies and wage tax declarations kept 5 years after the end of the calendar year in which the employment ended, as required by the wage tax rules; payment files deleted after execution
governance.sharingPolicy: wage tax returns filed with the Belastingdienst; payslips delivered to the employee; pension data shared with the client's pension provider at the client's instruction; internal otherwise and never shared with ecosystem partners

assets.name: Filing Submission
assets.description: The record of one transmission to an authority through the official digital channels: the submission type (VAT return, ICP declaration, income tax return, corporate tax return, wage tax return, KVK annual accounts deposit, KVK data change), the entity and period, the intermediary authorisation used, the payload reference and hash, timestamps of hand-off, transport acknowledgement and processing response from the Belastingdienst or KVK, error codes and retry history, the bookkeeper who released it, the deadline it was filed against and the proof of timely filing. Mastered by the Belastingdienst Filing Gateway (bdgw), created for KVK deposits by KVK Filing and Company Data (kvkf) and for wage tax by Payroll and Payslips (payr), and transported by the Integration and API Gateway (intg).
assets.businessMeaning: The proof that a return was filed on time: when the Belastingdienst imposes a late-filing penalty, this record is what the bookkeeper uses to show the client was not late.
assets.accessScope: the filing and integrations team for transport diagnostics; the releasing bookkeeper and backup for status; the client for the acknowledgement of their own filing; payload content readable only through the return it belongs to

interfaces.name: filing-submission api
interfaces.description: Submission creation, payload validation against the authority schema, release by bookkeeper, transport, acknowledgement polling, error handling and retry, proof-of-filing retrieval and batch status API used by VAT, income tax, corporate tax, payroll, KVK filing, deadline orchestration and the bookkeeper workspace.

interfaces.name: filing events
interfaces.description: Submission released, accepted by transport, processed by authority, rejected with error, retried and proof-of-filing stored events consumed by deadline orchestration, notifications, the return modules, QA and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: authority message exchange
interfaces.description: Outbound messages in the Belastingdienst and KVK digital formats and the inbound acknowledgements, assessments and rejection reports stored with the submission.

governance.retention: kept 7 years after the fiscal year of the filing with the acknowledgement as proof of timely filing; transport logs with technical detail kept 2 years; certificates and authorisations managed separately in the vault
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with the Belastingdienst and KVK under the company's intermediary authorisation and certificates; acknowledgement shared with the client; never shared with partners

rootGroups.name: Bookkeeper Workflow and Quality Data
rootGroups.description: The operational data of the roughly forty bookkeepers in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht: the filing calendar and deadlines per client, the review tasks that flow through each bookkeeper's queue, the allocation of clients to bookkeepers and backups, the messages and calls with clients, the four-eyes quality findings and the advice knowledge base that keeps tax answers consistent. This data decides how many clients one bookkeeper can serve well, which is the productivity lever behind scaling from 10,000 to 20,000 clients without losing the personal bookkeeper.

subGroups.name: Review, Deadlines and Allocation
subGroups.description: The workload machinery: deadlines per entity and filing type, the review tasks derived from them and from client activity, and the client-to-bookkeeper allocation with backup coverage per office.

assets.name: Filing Deadline
assets.description: A statutory or internal deadline for one entity: the quarterly VAT return due on the last day of the month after the quarter, the income tax return season with any intermediary extension granted, corporate tax filing dates for BVs, the KVK deposit deadline for statutory accounts, monthly wage tax returns, Ponto re-authorisation expiry, and the internal milestones Kees sets before each (receipts requested, bookkeeper check complete, client approval, release), with the calendar rules that generated it, exceptions per entity, the current status and the responsible bookkeeper. Maintained by Filing Calendar and Deadline Orchestration (dlin) and surfaced to clients by Deadlines, To-dos and Notifications (ntfy).
assets.businessMeaning: The clock every bookkeeper works against: on-time filing is the promise of the service, and the calendar is what turns 10,000 individual deadlines into a plannable workload.
assets.accessScope: the assigned bookkeeper, backup and team leads; the client for their own deadlines; the bookkeeper workspace team and the quality team for calendar rules and escalation reporting

interfaces.name: filing-deadline api
interfaces.description: Calendar-rule evaluation per entity and filing type, extension registration, internal milestone generation, status and escalation, and per-bookkeeper and per-office deadline overview API used by deadline orchestration, the review queue, workload planning, notifications and the client app.

interfaces.name: deadline events
interfaces.description: Deadline generated, milestone due, milestone missed, extension granted, deadline met and deadline escalated to team lead events consumed by the review queue, notifications, workload planning and on-time reporting.

governance.retention: deadlines and their met or missed status kept 7 years with the filing they governed as evidence of timeliness; internal milestones kept 2 years for productivity analysis
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; the client sees their own deadlines; never shared with partners

assets.name: Review Task
assets.description: One item of bookkeeper work in the client file: check the bookings of a quarter, resolve unmatched bank transactions, request missing receipts, answer a client question, prepare or release a return, run a year-end checklist item, complete a four-eyes check requested by QA or handle a switch import; with the client and entity, priority and due date derived from the filing deadline, the assigned bookkeeper or backup, status (open, waiting for client, in review, done), time spent, the objects it refers to and the outcome. Mastered by the Bookkeeper Client File and Review Queue (bkws), scheduled by Filing Calendar and Deadline Orchestration (dlin) and sampled by Quality Assurance and Four-eyes Checks (qaud).
assets.businessMeaning: The unit of bookkeeper productivity: review turnaround and clients served per bookkeeper are measured on these tasks, and the queue is what lets a colleague take over seamlessly when a bookkeeper is out.
assets.accessScope: the assigned bookkeeper, backup and team leads for their portfolio and office; QA specialists for sampled tasks; the bookkeeper workspace team for queue diagnostics; the client sees only the tasks waiting on them

interfaces.name: review-task api
interfaces.description: Task creation from deadlines and client activity, prioritisation, assignment and hand-over to backup, status transitions, time tracking, waiting-for-client requests and portfolio overview API used by the review queue, deadline orchestration, QA sampling, client messaging and workload planning.

interfaces.name: review task events
interfaces.description: Task created, assigned, handed over, waiting for client, completed, overdue and selected for four-eyes check events consumed by notifications, QA, workload planning and productivity dashboards.

governance.retention: kept 2 years after completion for productivity and quality analysis, then reduced to counts; tasks that record a fiscal decision are referenced from the audit trail and follow its 7-year retention
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; the client sees only requests addressed to them; never shared with partners

assets.name: Client Allocation
assets.description: The assignment of a client to a personal bookkeeper and a backup colleague within one of the three offices: effective dates, the reason (new client, bookkeeper leaving or on leave, portfolio rebalancing, legal-form change to Founders, client request), the bookkeeper's portfolio size and complexity points (legal form, bank connections, payroll, VOF partners, switch import), the office capacity plan and team-lead approvals, and the history of previous assignments. Managed by Client Allocation and Workload Planning (wkld) and set for the first time by Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching (onbd) when a new client is matched.
assets.businessMeaning: The decision of who serves whom: matching a creative freelancer with a bookkeeper who understands creative work is part of the proposition, and portfolio balance is how capacity is planned as a product.
assets.accessScope: team leads and the Head of Operations for their offices; the assigned bookkeeper and backup for their own portfolio; client success for matching; the client sees the name and contact of their bookkeeper only

interfaces.name: client-allocation api
interfaces.description: Assignment and reassignment, backup designation, portfolio and complexity-point calculation, office capacity view and matching-suggestion API used by workload planning, onboarding, the review queue, client messaging and the client app's bookkeeper card.

interfaces.name: allocation events
interfaces.description: Client assigned, reassigned, backup activated, portfolio over capacity and bookkeeper leaving events consumed by the review queue, notifications to the client, client success and capacity dashboards.

governance.retention: allocation history kept for the life of the client relationship and 7 years after, because it shows which bookkeeper was responsible for each filing; capacity plans kept 3 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; the client is told who their bookkeeper and backup are; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Communication, Quality and Knowledge
subGroups.description: Everything said between client and bookkeeper, the four-eyes findings that measure first-time-right quality, and the advice knowledge base that keeps tax answers consistent across bookkeepers and offices.

assets.name: Client Message
assets.description: One interaction between a client and Kees: an in-app or e-mail message thread with the bookkeeper (questions about deductions, an unclear transaction, a request to send receipts), a logged phone call with notes, a scheduled video or in-person meeting, a proactive update from the bookkeeper about a deadline or rule change, or an escalation to a fiscal specialist; with participants, channel, timestamps, attachments, the client file objects referenced, the knowledge-base article cited in the answer, response time and resolution state. Mastered by Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log (msgc) in the bookkeeping pods and enriched by the Advice Knowledge Base and Tax Rules Content (advk) with suggested answers.
assets.businessMeaning: The personal bookkeeper relationship in data form: answered questions are the reason clients stay, and response time is the metric that shows whether scale is hurting the relationship.
assets.accessScope: the client and their partners for their own threads; the assigned bookkeeper and backup; team leads and fiscal specialists on escalation; the quality team for anonymised samples used in training

interfaces.name: client-message api
interfaces.description: Thread creation, e-mail send and receive, call logging, meeting scheduling through Google Meet, attachment handling, suggested-answer lookup, escalation and response-time reporting API used by the bookkeeper workspace, the client app, the mobile app, the knowledge base and client success.

interfaces.name: client message events
interfaces.description: Message received, answered, escalated to specialist, meeting scheduled, unanswered for 2 business days and thread closed events consumed by the review queue, notifications, team-lead dashboards and knowledge-gap analysis.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the client relationship and 7 years after where the thread documents a fiscal decision or instruction; casual threads deleted 2 years after closure; call recordings are not made
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the client and Kees de Boekhouder or Founders; e-mail and meeting providers act as processors; anonymised excerpts used for internal training only; never shared with partners

assets.name: QA Finding
assets.description: The result of one four-eyes check or quality sample: the client file, return or year-end package examined, the checking bookkeeper or QA specialist, the checklist applied (VAT boxes, deductions and hours criterion, private-use splits, VOF split, BV intercompany positions, payroll), each finding with severity (blocking before release, correct after filing, coaching point), the root cause category (recognition error, missing receipt, rule misapplied, client information late, calendar issue), the correction made and the training follow-up for the bookkeeper. Produced by Quality Assurance and Four-eyes Checks (qaud) on tasks selected from the review queue and reported to the Head of QA.
assets.businessMeaning: How first-time-right quality is measured and improved: findings tell the quality team which rules bookkeepers get wrong and where the software should catch the error before a human does.
assets.accessScope: the Head of QA and fiscal specialists; the checked bookkeeper for their own findings; team leads for their office; the client only through the corrected return, never the finding itself

interfaces.name: qa-finding api
interfaces.description: Sample selection, checklist execution, finding registration with severity and root cause, correction linking, bookkeeper feedback and first-time-right reporting per bookkeeper, office and rule API used by the QA module, the review queue, the knowledge base and team-lead dashboards.

interfaces.name: qa events
interfaces.description: Sample selected, blocking finding raised, release blocked, finding resolved and recurring root cause detected events consumed by the review queue, the return modules, the knowledge base backlog and quality dashboards.

governance.retention: findings on filed returns kept 7 years with the return they concern; coaching findings about a bookkeeper kept 2 years and then anonymised into quality statistics, in line with employee data rules
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Kees de Boekhouder and Founders; findings about a bookkeeper treated as employee data with access limited to the QA team and their team lead; never shared with clients or partners

assets.name: Tax Rule Article
assets.description: A curated article in the advice knowledge base: a tax rule or entrepreneur topic explained for bookkeepers and clients, such as zelfstandigenaftrek (€1,200 in 2026, €900 in 2027), startersaftrek (€2,123), mkb-winstvrijstelling, the hours criterion, KOR up to €20,000 turnover, VAT rates and reverse charge, buying a house as a freelancer, entrepreneurship next to a job, Wet DBA enforcement since 1 January 2025, DGA customary salary, or the eenmanszaak-to-BV decision; with the rule values per tax year, effective dates, sources, the bookkeeper-facing answer template, the client-facing explanation, the related booking rules and calendar rules in the engine, review owner and last review date. Maintained by Advice Knowledge Base and Tax Rules Content (advk) under the quality and tax knowledge team and cited from Client Messaging (msgc).
assets.businessMeaning: The reason 45 bookkeepers in three offices give the same answer: the knowledge base is what makes proactive, consistent advice a scalable differentiator against software-only competitors.
assets.accessScope: all bookkeepers and client success staff read; fiscal specialists in the quality team author and approve; selected client-facing explanations published in the app and the Keep up content; no client data inside

interfaces.name: tax-rule-article api
interfaces.description: Article authoring, per-tax-year rule values, approval and versioning, search and suggested-answer retrieval, rule-value publication to the bookkeeping engine and client-facing publication API used by the knowledge base, client messaging, the ledger and return modules, the client app and content marketing.

interfaces.name: knowledge events
interfaces.description: Article published, rule value changed for a new tax year, article due for review and knowledge gap reported from messaging or QA events consumed by the bookkeeping engine, notifications to clients affected by a change, the QA team and content marketing.

interfaces.name: knowledge exports
interfaces.description: PDF and web exports of client-facing explanations for the app, the blog and partner member pages, and the per-tax-year rule table exported for the bookkeeping engine's configuration review.

governance.retention: all versions kept indefinitely because a return filed in a past year must be explained with the rule values of that year; superseded versions marked with their validity period
governance.sharingPolicy: internal articles for Kees and Founders staff; client-facing explanations public on the website and in the app; rule values shared with partners' member pages in generic form only

rootGroups.name: Growth and Client Lifecycle Data
rootGroups.description: The data that grows and keeps the client base: website leads and the free Google Meet introductions, onboarding cases with the mutual-fit check and bookkeeper matching, the historical returns imported when a client switches from a previous bookkeeper, the fixed-fee subscription plans per legal form with their add-ons, the monthly subscription invoices, the partner programme with member benefits and referral tracking, and the entrepreneur network profiles and client stories that turn satisfied clients into ambassadors. Marketing data here is kept deliberately separate from the administration data: a lead's details never become part of a client file until the client signs.

subGroups.name: Leads, Partners and Community
subGroups.description: Top of the funnel and the community around it: leads and intro calls, referral benefits through professional associations and service partners, and the public-facing network profiles and client stories.

assets.name: Lead and Intro Call
assets.description: A prospective client from first contact to decision: name, e-mail, phone, KVK status (registered, planning to register, switching from another bookkeeper), intended legal form and sector (creative, knowledge work, starter next to a job, VOF, BV), the acquisition channel and partner or referring client, the free Google Meet introduction booked from the website with date, sales executive and outcome notes, the mutual-fit assessment (administration size, expectations, whether the client accepts that external accounting software is not supported), the plan quoted, marketing consent and follow-up sequence, and the conversion to an onboarding case or the reason for not proceeding. Captured by Lead Capture and Intro Call Booking (lead) and handed to Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching on a positive fit check.
assets.businessMeaning: The top of the growth engine toward 20,000 clients: intro-to-active conversion and channel attribution are measured here, and the fit check protects bookkeepers from clients the model cannot serve well.
assets.accessScope: sales and client success executives; the Head of Growth and marketing for channel attribution in aggregated form; never visible to bookkeepers until the lead becomes an onboarding case

interfaces.name: lead api
interfaces.description: Website form and appointment capture, Google Meet scheduling, channel and referral attribution, fit-check outcome, plan quote, follow-up sequence and convert-to-onboarding API used by the public website, the sales workspace, the partner programme and growth analytics.

interfaces.name: lead events
interfaces.description: Lead created, intro call booked, intro call held, fit check passed or failed, converted to onboarding and lost events consumed by onboarding, the partner programme's referral tracking, marketing automation and conversion dashboards.

governance.retention: leads that do not convert deleted 12 months after the last contact unless marketing consent is renewed; converted leads reduced to attribution data once the onboarding case is created; intro call notes never copied into the client file
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the growth and client success teams; referral status reported back to the referring partner as counts, never as named leads, unless the lead consented to the partner benefit; never sold

assets.name: Partner Referral
assets.description: The link between an ecosystem partner and a Kees client or lead: the partner (BNO, DuPho, Kunstenbond, Stichting BOK, voordekunst, Unfair, Insify, BrightPensioen, DAS) and the agreement terms, the member benefit offered (for example no administration costs plus three months free for Stichting BOK members, a €50 discount with BrightPensioen), the referral code or landing page used, the member or client who claimed it with their consent to share the claim with the partner, the direction (partner refers member to Kees, or Kees refers client to a partner's insurance, pension or legal product), the benefit status (claimed, verified, applied to subscription, expired) and the attribution to a subscription. Managed by Partner Programme and Referral Benefits (prtn) and applied to the client's subscription through the client account.
assets.businessMeaning: The mechanism that lowers acquisition cost and makes Kees the financial home of the freelancer: every verified referral is both a cheaper client and a partner relationship kept alive.
assets.accessScope: the growth and partnerships team; client success for applying benefits; the client for their own claimed benefits; partner contacts see aggregated counts and, with consent, the claims of their own members

interfaces.name: partner-referral api
interfaces.description: Partner agreement and benefit catalogue, referral code and landing page generation, benefit claim and membership verification, consent capture, subscription discount application and partner reporting API used by the public website, onboarding, subscription billing and the partner portal.

interfaces.name: referral events
interfaces.description: Benefit claimed, membership verified, discount applied, referral converted to active client, benefit expired and partner agreement changed events consumed by subscription billing, lead attribution, notifications and partner reporting.

interfaces.name: partner reports
interfaces.description: Periodic referral and uptake reports per partner in PDF and CSV with counts and, where members consented, the claims of their own members, and the benefit catalogue exported to partner member pages.

governance.retention: referral records kept for the life of the partner agreement and 3 years after for reconciliation of benefits; consent records kept as long as the claim is reported to the partner; claims by non-converting leads deleted with the lead
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the partner only for the member who consented and otherwise as aggregated counts; internal to growth and client success; never used for the partner's own marketing without the member's consent

assets.name: Entrepreneur Network Profile
assets.description: The opt-in public profile of a client in the Kees entrepreneur network and the client stories built from it: display name and trading name, profession and sector, city, website and social links, a short bio and portfolio images the client uploads, the network categories they want to be found in, visibility settings, and where the client agreed, the client story or video testimonial (as with Jochem, Celeste, Nathalie, Yoeri and Elin, Tynke and Marloes) with the consent record, publication channels (website, blog, Keep up content, social) and the review status by marketing. Managed by Entrepreneur Network Profiles and Client Stories (cnet), always separate from the administration and visible only to the extent the client chose.
assets.businessMeaning: The community layer that turns loyal clients into ambassadors: profiles and stories are the word-of-mouth engine Vortex singled out, and they only work because they are fully in the client's control.
assets.accessScope: the client edits their own profile and consents; marketing reviews and publishes; other network members and the public see only what the profile's visibility allows; bookkeepers do not need access

interfaces.name: network-profile api
interfaces.description: Profile creation, portfolio upload, category and visibility settings, consent for stories and testimonials, publication review and network search API used by the client app, the public website and marketing tooling.

interfaces.name: network events
interfaces.description: Profile published, visibility changed, story consent given or withdrawn, story published and profile removed events consumed by the public website, content marketing and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: story and media outputs
interfaces.description: Approved client stories, photos and video testimonials exported to the website, blog and social channels, and the profile data the client can download or delete.

governance.retention: kept while the client keeps the profile published; removed within 30 days of the client withdrawing or leaving; published stories taken down on withdrawal of consent and archived internally only as a consent record
governance.sharingPolicy: public to the extent the client chose; stories shared on Kees channels and, with the client's consent, on partner channels; never shared with the Belastingdienst or used in the administration

subGroups.name: Onboarding and Subscription
subGroups.description: From signed client to billed subscription: the onboarding case with fit check and bookkeeper matching, the historical returns imported from a previous bookkeeper, the plan catalogue per legal form and the monthly subscription invoices with add-ons.

assets.name: Onboarding Case
